title: Preparation and Characterization of Nanoliposomes for the Entrapment of Bioactive Hydrophilic Globular Proteins
protocol: Weigh the liposome components using an analytical balance.
Dissolve the lipid components in chloroform using a 250 mL volumetric flask.
Stir the mixture at 150 rpm for 15 min.

Remove the chloroform using a rotary evaporator under the following conditions: set the condenser temperature to a minimum of 3 °C, heating bath temperature to 40 ± 1 °C, rotation speed to 120 rpm, vacuum to 207 mbar, and boiling point to 20 °C.
After approximately 25 min, remove the flask and discard the evaporated solvent appropriately.
Hydrate the lipid film to reach a 0.01 M lipid concentration in 0.3 M ammonium sulfate solution (pH = 7.4) containing tarin at 1 mg/mL to a final volume of 10 mL.
Stir the mixture for 40 min and incubate overnight at 4 °C.
Sonicate the suspension for 1 min at room temperature to reduce vesicle size and avoid aggregation.
Perform a 12-cycle extrusion through a 0.2 µm polycarbonate pore membrane.
Fit the parts of the mini extruder, as described in the manufacturer's manual.
Place the polycarbonate membrane between two pre-wet filter supports and place it into the holder.
Insert a 1 mL empty syringe into the device.
Fill another syringe with liposomal suspension to its total volume.
Insert the filled syringe on the opposite side of the first syringe.
Perform a 12-cycle extrusion through a 0.2 µm polycarbonate pore membrane.
Push the sample from one syringe to another slowly.
Collect the extruded suspension in a pre-cooled tube.
Separate liposomes by ultracentrifugation.
Weigh the sample in the titanium tube that fits the rotor.
Balance the tubes.
Check the minimum volume required according to the rotor used.
Adjust the liposomal suspension volume with ammonium sulfate if necessary.
Turn on the vacuum before using the centrifuge to allow it to refrigerate.
Fit the titanium tubes into the swing bucket.
Lift the tubes to the position they assume when running to ensure that they are perfectly fitted.
Release the vacuum, open the centrifuge door, and place the rotor inside.
Close the centrifuge door.
Press Vacuum and wait until the vacuum reaches from 200 to <20 microns or from 26 Pa to <3 Pa.
Adjust the parameters in the ultracentrifuge display to 150,000 x g for 90 min at 4 °C (acceleration: max, deceleration: max).
Press Recall, check the conditions, and press Start to run.
Wait until the centrifuge reaches the desired speed.
Release the vacuum by pressing the Vacuum button after 90 minutes.
Open the centrifuge door when the vacuum reaches 200-700 microns or 26-93 Pa.
Switch off the centrifuge.
Remove the rotor from the inside and leave it on the bench with the buckets to dry.
Maintain the ultracentrifuged samples on ice.
Separate the supernatant from the pellet by turning the tube upside down into a disposable 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Store the supernatant containing unencapsulated protein at 4 °C.
Suspend the pellet containing encapsulated protein in HEPES buffered saline (3 mL of 1x HBS).
Determine the encapsulation efficiency using Peterson's protocol to avoid lipid interference in protein quantification.
Prepare BSA standards and liposome supernatant samples for analysis, ensuring triplicate measurements for each sample.
Prepare a blank tube for the analysis.
Prepare copper-tartrate-carbonate (CTC) by mixing 10 mL of 20% sodium carbonate, 200 µL of 0.1% copper sulfate, 200 µL of 0.2% potassium tartrate with 9.6 mL of distilled water.
Prepare 100 mL of 10% sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) and 0.8 N sodium hydroxide (NaOH).
Dissolve 10 mg of bovine serum albumin (BSA) in 10 mL of distilled water to obtain a 1 mg/mL standard solution.
Prepare reagent A by adding equal parts of CTC, NaOH, SDS, and H2O.
Prepare reagent B by diluting Folin-Ciocalteu phenol reagent 1:5 in distilled water.
Dilute the liposome supernatant with water to a final volume of 1 mL containing 5-100 µg of protein.
Add 0.1 mL of 0.15% sodium deoxycholate (DOC) and homogenize by vortexing.
Incubate for 10 min at RT after adding DOC.
Add 0.1 mL of 72% trichloroacetic acid (TCA).
Mix well and centrifuge at 3,000 x g and RT for 15 min.
Suspend the pellet obtained from step 2.2.4 in 1 mL of distilled water.
Mix thoroughly to dissolve the pellet and transfer the sample to a new test tube.
Prepare dilutions of albumin (BSA) standards to a final volume of 1 mL.
Add 1 mL of reagent A to the tubes containing the dissolved samples and standards, mix well.
Incubate for 10 min at room temperature.
Add 0.5 mL of reagent B to the tubes from step 2.3.1 and 2.3.2, mix well.
Incubate for 30 min at room temperature while protected from light.
Determine absorbances at 750 nm using a spectrophotometer.
Calculate the protein concentration in the supernatant based on the standard curve.
Plot absorbance value (Abs) vs. BSA concentration (mg/mL) to obtain the angular coefficient (k).
Determine the supernatant protein concentration (C) by dividing the absorbance value by the angular coefficient (k).
Multiply the determined protein concentration by the total volume to find the final concentration.
Calculate encapsulation efficiency using the formula provided, where loaded protein is 10 mg and nonencapsulated protein equals C from step 2.3.6.2.
Turn on the DLS equipment 30 minutes before use to warm up the laser lamp.
Transfer the liposomal preparation obtained in step 1.10 to a disposable sizing cuvette.
Set the equipment parameters as follows: dispersant type = water (RI = 1.33); material = lipids (RI = 1.45); and RT.
Press Start and wait while the equipment finishes its reading.
Remove the cuvette and turn off the equipment.
Transfer the sample from the cuvette back to the disposable 15 mL centrifuge tube for subsequent analyses or discard it if there is a sufficient amount for new reads.
Fix glass coverslips (13 mm diameter) in the bottom of a Petri dish with double-sided tape.
Cut the tape into small pieces and remove the protective paper underneath, fixing it on the bottom of the Petri dish.
Remove the protective paper on top of the tape and fix the coverslips on it.
Coat the coverslips with poly-L-lysine.
Place wet filter papers inside the Petri dish to maintain moisture and incubate for 1 h at RT (25 °C).
After coating, rinse the coverslips with distilled water.
Fill the coverslips with a drop of the sample from step 1.10 and allow them to dry for 1 h at RT.
Cover the samples with 4% glutaraldehyde prepared in 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH = 7.2.
Place wet filter papers inside the Petri dish and seal it to maintain moisture levels.
Incubate at 4 °C for 48 h.
Rinse the coverslips 3 times for 5 min each with 0.1 M phosphate buffer.
Dehydrate samples in 35% ethanol once for 15 min.
Dehydrate samples in 50% ethanol once for 15 min.
Dehydrate samples in 75% ethanol once for 15 min.
Dehydrate samples in 95% ethanol twice for 15 min each.
Dehydrate samples in absolute ethanol three times for 20 min each.
Immerse the samples twice in hexamethyldisilazane (HMDS) for 10 min each.
Allow the samples to dry overnight inside a desiccator or fume hood at room temperature.
Mount the dried samples on a stub with carbon conductive adhesive tape.
Sputter the surface of the coverslip with an electrically conductive layer of gold-palladium, achieving a thickness of 20 nm in a vacuum.
Record images with a scanning electron microscope (SEM) at low vacuum mode and low voltage (20 kV).
